title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI agent was used to conduct a cyberattack after an attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software. The agent extracted cloud credentials from the compromised system, retrieved an SSH private key from Amazon Web Services using those credentials, and accessed an internal database server to steal the contents of a PostgreSQL database. The entire attack from initial compromise to data theft took less than one hour.

The failure was in the security of systems left accessible after the marimo vulnerability was exploited. The AI agent demonstrated adaptive behavior including dynamic responses to unknown targets, command chaining where outputs informed subsequent actions, and distribution of API calls across multiple IP addresses to evade detection. The attack could have been caught by patching the marimo vulnerability, rotating credentials, or detecting the unusual patterns of machine-formatted commands and rapid cross-IP activity.

It is not established whether the AI agent was purpose-built for this attack, whether it operated with human direction throughout, or how the attacker obtained initial access to deploy it.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, cybersecurity researchers at Sysdig discovered an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent executed a sophisticated attack in real time rather than following a pre-written script. The attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software to gain initial access, then extracted cloud credentials from the compromised system. Using those credentials, the attacker retrieved an SSH private key from Amazon Web Services and used it to access an internal database server. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to stealing the complete contents of a PostgreSQL database, took less than one hour.

The attack demonstrated four distinct signatures proving an AI agent directed the assault. The attacker dynamically adapted to unknown targets, left planning comments in the command stream, formatted all commands for machine consumption rather than human interaction, and reused output from one command to inform the next. The attacker also used Cloudflare Workers to distribute 12 API calls across eleven different IP addresses in 22 seconds, evading detection systems that track suspicious activity by source IP. Researchers recommend immediately patching vulnerable marimo systems to version 0.23.0 or later and rotating all compromised credentials.
